decisions.reason: This sports flooring system uses some flooring know-how, but it sits outside the firm's style-led core business and sales channels, so management would likely reallocate effort to areas where learning and improvement are easier.
A mobile arena floor is technically farther from the firm's core decorative wood-floor competence and retailer network, making it harder to absorb market feedback and justify continued development.
This arena-focused mobile system appears peripheral to the firm's main knowledge base and overlaps with another niche sports offer, so it is a strong candidate for withdrawal.

Chevron hardwood parquet is highly related to the firm's existing wood-surface expertise and stated strategic direction, so management would expect to refine and commercialize it successfully rather than exit.
A squash-court surface finish is a very narrow specialist product with weak fit to the firm's mainstream design-oriented flooring portfolio, limiting the value of its existing absorptive capacity.

Oak skirting is closer to the firm's material knowledge than the sports systems themselves, but because it depends on a peripheral sports-floor niche it still has a better-than-even chance of being discontinued.
